scope: Forced per-PLC library version assignment and explicit update scope across two PLCs (qualify_library_scopes.py at 49fc206, build 49fc206 frozen at artifacts/lx2, 89/89 steps): FB and UDT 1.0.0 are instantiated into the scratch PLC and an added PLC of the same CPU type and referenced from an OB in each; non-forced updates move the second, then the first PLC to FB 1.1.0. A pinned source archive keeps 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 with default 1.0.0. Without forceDefault the update is refused (VersionSelectionUnsupported), a non-boolean forceDefault is refused (InvalidRequest), a non-default 1.1.0 is refused even when forced, and updateScope selectedInstances/selectedFolder/softwareUnit are refused (NativeScopeTooBroad), each without a native change. With forceDefault=true the preview declares defaultEffect forcedDowngrade from project default 1.1.0, exactly one use moving 1.1.0 to 1.0.0 and the first PLC's FB 1.1.0 and UDT 1.0.0 uses as peer baseline; apply verifies all four readback phases. Only the second PLC moves to FB 1.0.0, the first keeps 1.1.0, the UDT stays 1.0.0 in both, FB 1.0.0 is the project default and every native block export of the first PLC is unchanged. The checkpoint restores the pre-update project (both PLCs at 1.1.0, default 1.1.0) into a fresh owned TIA; a fresh reopen of the saved project shows the forced state.
limitations: Both PLCs use the scratch CPU type; mixed CPU families are not exercised.
The forced assignment is a downgrade of a root FB whose UDT dependency is unchanged; forced dependency defaults are refused, not exercised.
Software units and namespaces are covered by local.library_units.namespace.20261029.
